questions.title: Polymorphs are NOT a chronic inflammatory cell
questions.question: The following are NOT chronic inflammatory cells:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Macrophages are one of the three named chronic-inflammatory cells -- they are the key cell of chronic inflammation, not the excluded one.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Plasma cells (antibody-secreting B-lymphocyte derivatives) are also a chronic-inflammatory cell, part of the same triad as macrophages and lymphocytes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lymphocytes are the third member of the chronic-inflammatory-cell triad, activated to secrete the cytokines that sustain the chronic response.
explanations.D: Correct. Polymorphs (neutrophils) are the hallmark cell of acute, not chronic, inflammation. Chronic inflammation is instead dominated by mononuclear cells -- macrophages, lymphocytes and plasma cells -- so polymorphs are specifically the one NOT counted among the chronic inflammatory cells here.

questions.learning_objective: State that polymorphs (neutrophils), not macrophages, plasma cells or lymphocytes, are excluded from the chronic inflammatory cell types.

questions.title: Granuloma pathogenesis is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction
questions.question: Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of granuloma?

explanations.A: Incorrect. An atopic reaction is an immediate, IgE-mediated (type I) hypersensitivity response, not the T-cell-driven mechanism that builds a granuloma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A cytotoxic reaction (type II hypersensitivity) is antibody-mediated destruction of a target cell, an entirely different mechanism from granuloma formation.
explanations.C: Correct. Granuloma pathogenesis is a delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity reaction: a macrophage presents a persistent antigen to T lymphocytes, and the lymphokines they release activate and aggregate macrophages into the epithelioid-cell granuloma. This T-cell-mediated, delayed mechanism is what best explains how a granuloma forms.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Anaphylactic reactions are severe, immediate (type I) hypersensitivity responses, not the delayed, cell-mediated process underlying granuloma formation.

questions.learning_objective: State that granuloma pathogenesis is best explained by a delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity reaction.

questions.title: Bilharzial granuloma depends on type IV hypersensitivity
questions.question: Bilharzial granuloma depend on:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Type III (immune-complex) hypersensitivity is antigen-antibody complex deposition causing tissue damage, not the mechanism that builds the bilharzial granuloma around a schistosome ovum.
explanations.B: Correct. Like every granuloma, the bilharzial granuloma around a Schistosoma ovum forms through a type IV (delayed, T-cell-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction. Macrophages present ovum antigen to T lymphocytes, whose lymphokines activate and aggregate macrophages around the trapped egg. This is the same pathogenesis tested generically for granuloma formation, here applied to its bilharzial cause.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Type I (immediate, IgE-mediated) hypersensitivity underlies atopic and anaphylactic reactions, not the delayed, macrophage-driven granulomatous response to a schistosome ovum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Type II (antibody-mediated cytotoxic) hypersensitivity destroys a targeted cell directly, an unrelated mechanism from the T-cell/macrophage pathway that forms a granuloma.

questions.learning_objective: Apply the type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity mechanism of granuloma pathogenesis to the bilharzial granuloma specifically.
